questions.q: An ACL lists three roles in its Requires role related list. How many of those roles does a user need to satisfy the role check?
options: Exactly two of the three
All three roles at once
At least one of the three listed roles
None — the related list is informational only
questions.explain: Requires role works as an OR within the list itself — holding any one of the listed roles satisfies that part of the check.

questions.q: What happens to the role requirement on an ACL whose Requires role related list is empty?
options: Every user is required to be an administrator
The ACL automatically fails for every user
The role check is skipped entirely, not automatically failed
The ACL becomes a field-level ACL automatically
questions.explain: An empty Requires role list means there's no role requirement for that ACL — the check simply isn't applied.

questions.q: What must an ACL script do to grant access, since there's no implicit return value?
options: Nothing — scripts pass by default unless they throw an error
Explicitly set answer = true using the current record
Return true as the last line of the function
Call a separate grantAccess() API
questions.explain: ACL scripts must explicitly set the answer Boolean variable; if the script never sets it, the ACL does not grant access by default.

questions.q: Why might an admin use a script instead of the condition builder for an ACL like incident.assignment_group?
options: Scripts run faster than condition builders in every case
Scripts are required on every ACL regardless of logic complexity
The condition builder can't check something like group membership, which requires a lookup, not just a field comparison
Condition builders are deprecated in current ServiceNow versions
questions.explain: The simple condition builder only does direct field comparisons; checking whether the current user belongs to a referenced group needs a script.

questions.q: An ACL has both a required role and a script. A user holds the required role, but the script sets answer = false. Does the user pass this ACL?
options: Yes, because scripts are only advisory when a role is also listed
No, role and condition/script are combined with AND — both must pass
Yes, holding the required role is enough on its own
It depends on which was created first, the role list or the script
questions.explain: Role and condition/script combine with AND on a single ACL — failing either one fails the whole ACL, even if the other part passed.
